questions.key_step: Show f' vanishes at 1/2, 1, 3/2, then apply Rolle twice.
questions.justification: Rolle's theorem on f' after noticing the symmetric form; two applications - level 2 set from the key step (JEE Main standard, below the Advanced anchors).

questions.key_step: Increasing exponential on (-inf,-1] gives (a,b]=(0,e^3]; then point-line distance.
questions.justification: Monotonicity and range then a standard distance formula - routine, two short stages.

questions.key_step: Swap x and 1/x to solve the functional equation, then differentiate y.
questions.justification: Functional-equation elimination followed by a sign chart of a quartic derivative.

questions.key_step: Recognise the left side as (x ln x f - x)' and use monotonicity of the auxiliary function.
questions.justification: Hidden product rule plus careful endpoint bounds; the data are in fact inconsistent, which adds confusion.

questions.key_step: Simplify g to (1+e^x)/(1-e^x) and differentiate.
questions.justification: Direct simplification and a one-line derivative - routine.

questions.key_step: Sign of f' changes at +-1, so not monotone on R.
questions.justification: Quotient rule and sign scheme; standard.

questions.key_step: h=f-g has h''=6x; integrate twice with the two conditions and test each statement.
questions.justification: Four statements to verify after two integrations; routine but long.

questions.key_step: Identify f^2(3f'f''+ff''')=(f^3 f'')' and count zeros by Rolle.
questions.justification: Needs the integrating-factor idea plus careful root counting; the least routine question of the paper.

questions.key_step: f'=A sin4x+B has no zero iff |B|>|A|; exclude p=2.
questions.justification: One trigonometric-bound idea plus a degenerate case.

questions.key_step: Count crossings of 2^x with x^2 and with a line.
questions.justification: Graph-based counting with exponential versus polynomial; standard.

questions.key_step: Turning points of the quintic and sign of y at test points.
questions.justification: Standard root counting with a quartic derivative solved by the quadratic formula.

questions.key_step: Peak of x^3/(x^4+147) at sqrt21; compare integers 4 and 5.
questions.justification: Calculus on a continuous extension then integer comparison.

questions.key_step: Sign at -inf, 0, +inf gives two roots (palindromic check for exactness).
questions.justification: IVT on an exponential polynomial; a palindromic substitution is the neat route.

questions.key_step: Piecewise-linear modulus function: list slopes, find sign changes.
questions.justification: Nested modulus, four breakpoints; careful but routine.

questions.key_step: Factorise f', local max at the smaller root.
questions.justification: Direct factorisation and one equation.

questions.key_step: Two critical conditions fix a, b; compare f at x=-1 and the endpoints.
questions.justification: Parameter finding then absolute extrema with a log term.

questions.key_step: Leibniz rule gives f'=2x(x^2-3)(x^2-5)e^{-x^2}; sign chart.
questions.justification: Leibniz differentiation and a five-root sign chart.

questions.key_step: Open the modulus, check each join, find the parabola vertex.
questions.justification: Piecewise function with three kinds of candidate points.

questions.key_step: Single critical point on [2,4]; compare with the endpoints.
questions.justification: Routine closed-interval extrema.

questions.key_step: Parametrise by the tilt angle; area=8+10 sin2theta.
questions.justification: Geometry set-up with an angle plus a trigonometric maximum.
